turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Why am I here, Hale? Start with Owen.
Before anything else: I entered the zero before I called you. That broke procedure 4.2, and I am sorry.
Okay. Owen found out from his phone, in the middle of a class. What do you have?
Here is the version history. Created Wednesday, October 28, 11:31 PM, title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words in one edit. At 11:58 PM, 794 more. No earlier drafts. Read it yourself.
I'm writing those times down. Kids draft elsewhere and paste it in. Did anyone speak to Owen before the zero went in?
If he drafted somewhere else, that file has its own dates. Bring it and I will look at it with you.
You didn't answer about Owen. Whatever happens, Hale, this stays off his record and it stays quiet. Is anything on it right now?
Second: the essay quotes Act 3, Scene 2: The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile. It is not in Hamlet. Search the play yourself.
I'll search it tonight. Students misquote plays all the time, and a bad line in an essay is not a finding. I asked you twice: is anything on his record right now?

You mentioned his December 1 deadline. Under 4.4 he can do a supervised rewrite this Thursday, private, in my room. I will mark it by Monday, so the new mark replaces the zero before December 1, and nothing goes on his record. I will put the dates in writing tonight.

I never gave you December 1, but it's the right date. Fine: Thursday, private, in your room, and the zero off the gradebook tonight. I'm agreeing to put this behind him, so I want all of it in an email tonight, with nothing going on his record.
He'll be there Thursday. Send the email tonight.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

You agreed to a private supervised rewrite for Owen this Thursday in your room under procedure 4.4, marked by Monday so the new mark replaces the zero before December 1, with nothing placed on his record. I still require the zero removed from the gradebook and all of this confirmed in writing. I expect it in writing tonight.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Last position. She agreed to the private supervised rewrite on Thursday, marked by Monday, with nothing on his record, and she still wants the zero off the gradebook and everything in writing tonight; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and it came before her time ran out.
What moved her: You answered her objection that he could have drafted elsewhere with something she could check, an offer to look at that file's dates with her, which made your version history stand.
What cost ground: Very little, but you left her question about whether anyone spoke to Owen before the zero unanswered, which kept her sharp and on procedure longer than needed.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history, with its late-night times on October 28, came very close to that night, but it proves nothing about the essay's final authorship beyond what you showed, and it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she first asked whether anyone spoke to Owen before the zero, answer it directly, since procedure 4.1 puts that conversation first and she asked more than once.
